html:
A nerve disease caused by mercury poisoning, first officially identified in 1956 in the fishing town of Minamata in Kumamoto, southern Japan. It became the defining case of industrial pollution in postwar Japan.

The cause was the Chisso chemical factory, which from the 1930s released waste containing methylmercury into Minamata Bay. The mercury built up in fish and shellfish, the main food of local families. Cats danced and died first; then people lost feeling in their hands and feet, had trouble walking, seeing and speaking, and many died. Babies were born damaged by mercury their mothers had eaten.

The company and the state long denied the link; dumping went on until 1968, when the state finally named the factory as the cause. A second outbreak hit Niigata in 1965. Victims fought for compensation, and photographs by W. Eugene Smith brought the case to the world. Thousands were recognised as victims. The scandal drove Japan's pollution laws of 1970, and the 2013 United Nations treaty on mercury is named after the town.
sum: A nerve disease caused by mercury poisoning, first officially identified in 1956 in the fishing town of Minamata in Kumamoto, southern Japan. It became the defining case of industrial pollution in postwar Japan.
